title: Instalator școală: the whole computer lab from one USB stick
description: Runs from a USB stick and silently installs the ticked programs one by one: on Windows 8–11 and on Ubuntu, Linux Mint, Q4OS, antiX. Free, GPL-3.0.
og_description: One stick. The whole lab. Silent installs on Windows and Linux.
hero_lead: The program runs from a USB stick, lists the programs with checkboxes and installs them one by one, with no windows and no “Next”. On Windows 8–11 and on Linux.
hero_note: Free and open source (GPL-3.0) · no internet needed · Furnica and Cangurul included
ui_language_note: The program itself speaks Romanian; the demos show its real interface.
how_lead: Prepare the stick once, at home. In the lab, each computer takes one click.
how_step_home: At home, unzip the archive onto a stick. Next to the program sits a Windows (or Linux) folder with one folder per program: its installer and a short program.toml file that says which version it is and how to install it silently.
how_step_lab: In the lab, start Instalator.exe; Windows asks for administrator rights once. On Linux, type sh /media/…/instalator.sh in a terminal and enter the password once. The drive letter doesn't matter.
how_step_screen: On screen, you see what's missing and what's out of date. The program reads the installed version (from the registry on Windows, from dpkg on Linux) and compares it with the one on the stick: missing and outdated programs are already ticked, up-to-date ones are not.
how_step_install: Press “Instalează” and move on to the next computer. When you come back you see, next to each program, whether it succeeded, plus a summary. A log named after the computer stays on the stick.
how_step_class: Next lesson, students find the programs in the Start menu or the applications menu, with the same version on every computer. Furnica and Cangurul, the executors for learning algorithms, come on the stick already.

g1_text: Everything comes from the stick: the installers, the descriptions, even the fallback OpenGL for computers without a video driver. The network isn't used at all.
g2_text: msiexec runs with /qn /norestart, .exe installers with the silent switches from program.toml, apt-get with -y. The computer never restarts on its own.
g3_text: If an installer still waits for a click, after 30 minutes it is stopped together with the processes it started, and the queue moves on.
g4_name: One error doesn't stop the rest
g4_text: Each program gets its own result, and an error comes with its reason (the exit code, apt's message); the others keep installing.
g5_text: The installed version is read from the registry (both views on 64-bit), from dpkg or from the marker left by the installer, and compared with the one on the stick.
g6_text: If a program was put into the same folder some other way (from an .msi, say), the installer leaves it alone and tells you to uninstall it first.
g7_text: The stick keeps jurnal\COMPUTERNAME-date-time.txt with the system, the commands run and the result of each. On a write-protected stick, installing works without a log.
g8_text: Written in Rust, GPL-3.0. The code, the descriptions and the builds are public on GitHub, with SHA256 checksums for every archive.
win_msi_note: plus your own arguments, exactly as written
